Zebulun
ZEB-yoo-luhn
proper noun (figure / tribe)
Hebrew Zebulun (H2074) — "dwelling" or "honor" (Gen 30:20); the tenth son of Jacob and the sixth of Leah; tribal patriarch of Zebulun, whose territory in Galilee bordered Naphtali and became part of the Isaiah 9 / Matthew 4 great-light prophecy fulfilled in Christ.

📖 Biblical Definition

Zebulun is the sixth and last son of Leah (Gen 30:19-20), born after Issachar; Leah named him with the hope "Now will my husband dwell with me, because I have born him six sons" (Gen 30:20). The Hebrew Zebulun is variously translated "dwelling" or "honor" depending on which root is emphasized (zabal = to dwell, exalt). Leah's naming preserves her long-running hope that bearing more sons would secure Jacob's love — six sons by her own womb, and still the prayer continues. Zebulun's tribe received territory in Galilee bordering Naphtali (Josh 19:10-16). Jacob's blessing was striking: "Zebulun shall dwell at the haven of the sea; and he shall be for an haven of ships; and his border shall be unto Zidon" (Gen 49:13) — a maritime-trade prophecy for a tribe whose actual territory was somewhat inland from the coast, suggesting that Zebulunite activity reached down to the Mediterranean trade routes via the coastal plain. Moses's blessing pairs Zebulun with Issachar: "Rejoice, Zebulun, in thy going out; and, Issachar, in thy tents" (Deut 33:18) — Zebulun the active outgoer, Issachar the settled tent-dweller, two complementary tribes. The most weighty Zebulun reference is Isaiah 9:1-2 (same passage as Naphtali): "the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali... the people that walked in darkness have seen a great light" — fulfilled at Matthew 4:13-16 when Christ began His public ministry in Galilee. The maritime tribe whose name meant DWELLING received the dwelling of God-with-us (Immanuel) walking its shore.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

Tenth son of Jacob, sixth of Leah; "dwelling" (Gen 30:20); tribe whose Galilean territory became part of Christ's ministry headquarters (Isa 9:1-2; Matt 4:13-16).

ZEBULUN, noun. (1) The tenth son of Jacob, sixth and last son of Leah (Gen 30:20). (2) The tribe descended from him, settled in Galilee bordering Naphtali (Josh 19:10-16).

Hebrew Zebulun — "dwelling" / "honor." Jacob's blessing prophesied maritime trade (Gen 49:13). Tribal territory was the focus, with Naphtali, of Isaiah 9:1-2's great-light prophecy fulfilled in Matt 4:13-16.

📖 Key Scripture

Genesis 30:19-20 — "And Leah conceived again, and bare Jacob the sixth son. And Leah said, God hath endued me with a good dowry; now will my husband dwell with me, because I have born him six sons: and she called his name Zebulun."

Genesis 49:13 — "Zebulun shall dwell at the haven of the sea; and he shall be for an haven of ships; and his border shall be unto Zidon."

Deuteronomy 33:18 — "And of Zebulun he said, Rejoice, Zebulun, in thy going out; and, Issachar, in thy tents."

Matthew 4:13-15 — "And leaving Nazareth, he came and dwelt in Capernaum, which is upon the sea coast, in the borders of Zabulon and Nephthalim: That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by Esaias the prophet, saying, The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Zebulun is corrupted when the Isa 9 / Matt 4 fulfillment is detached from the tribal-name layer (the Spirit deliberately named Zebulun and Naphtali in both prophecy and fulfillment), or when the maritime-trade blessing is dismissed as primitive geography rather than received as God's providence for a Galilean trading culture.

expand to see more

Prophecy-tribe severance. Isaiah 9:1-2 names Zebulun and Naphtali by name; Matthew 4:13-16 cites the prophecy and locates Christ's ministry exactly there. The Spirit chose tribal names in the prophecy (not just "Galilee") and Matthew preserves them. To strip the tribal layer is to lose the precision of Spirit-given fulfillment: not generic "Christ ministered in Galilee" but specifically in Zebulun's and Naphtali's tribal lands. The covenant continuity from Jacob's blessing to Christ's ministry runs through the named tribes.

Geography-only reading. Zebulun's maritime blessing ("shall dwell at the haven of the sea... haven of ships") is sometimes treated as approximate geographic poetry — Zebulun's actual inheritance lay somewhat inland. But the Galilean trading routes (the Way of the Sea, Via Maris) ran through Zebulunite territory, and Zebulunites were active in the Mediterranean trade economy of antiquity. The blessing was prophetic of CONNECTION rather than coastal possession — and Christ would later use those same trade routes as His ministry corridor.

Usage

"Zebulun means DWELLING — Leah's hope that bearing six sons would make Jacob dwell with her."
